page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dasv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This virtual machine operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate highly competitive single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and bzip3 single-threaded decompression, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, falls within the average range. Cryptographic and compression tasks are strong, with passmark CPU encryption and gzip single-threaded compression ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is also robust, with a strong PassMark memory score, though raw uncached read and write bandwidth benchmarks remain average. For machine learning workloads, the server delivers top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M LLM models, but performance drops to the bottom 10% when executing text generation on large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32as_v7 offers a balanced resource density suitable for general-purpose enterprise applications. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a stable foundation for workloads that require a mix of compute and memory without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of local storage requires external storage provisioning, which should be factored into architectural planning. This server is well-suited for applications such as web serving, database operations, moderate-scale data processing, and running lightweight machine learning inference models.
